findings.text: the paragraph attributes 21,359 kernel events per call and 36.83 ms of device time (and at :111 82.07 ms with 20.5 ms per slice, and at :110 165 events and 0.27 ms) to 'the twelve largest kernels', but those are the STEADY line's ALL-kernel sums (rebuilding_events 64077/3 = 21,359, rebuilding_ns 36.83 ms, carried 495/3 = 165 events and 0.27 ms, batch4 82.07 ms in logs/profile_kernels.log), whereas the twelve printed SINGLE_KERNEL / CARRIED_KERNEL / BATCH_KERNEL rows sum to 18,516 events and 31.3 ms, 58 events and 0.1 ms, and 19,587 events and 44.0 ms, so a reader summing the tabulated twelve rows gets different numbers than the sentence states.

the new '# command:' line emits SELECT unquoted, so the line it labels as the invocation a reader could re-run is not re-runnable: bash parses 'SELECT=limited and boundary or limited and read <script>' as running the command 'and' (measured: 'bash: line 1: and: command not found', EXIT=127). The progress the commit claims is real for WT/LOG but SELECT needs quoting (the '# exec:' line at :78 does carry it quoted).

test_logs and artifacts omit logs/negative_oracle2.log, the only control run at the reviewed head bc50440cb (revision header on its line 1, EXIT=1 at line 55: head 6 passed exit 0, mutant 3 failed exit 1), which is the run that exercises the changed run_boundary_mutant.sh header and default SELECT; the manifest's negative_control_log still names negative_oracle.log from an earlier revision, and the manifest (mtime 21:09) predates negative_oracle2.log (21:28), so the head's control is unrecorded for promotion's receipt.
